Container.Name: LightHue
Container.Overview:
Drives Philips Hue lights with the flicker patterns of twenty classic games, through a small web UI that several people on your network can use at once.
Quake's lightstyle table is here verbatim from id Software's released source, shared with Quake II, Half-Life and Source which ship it unchanged, plus hand-authored takes on DOOM, Heretic, Hexen, Descent, Marathon, Rise of the Triad, Duke Nukem 3D, Blood, Shadow Warrior, Thief, System Shock 2, Doom 3, Quake 4, Deus Ex and Unreal. Every preset carries the speed, brightness range and colour it was written for, so picking one brings its timing with it.
Pick lights, pattern, speed, brightness and colour, and change any of it while the lights are still running. Write your own a-z lightstyle strings with a live waveform preview, and export them to a small JSON file to share.
Build entertainment areas on the bridge and stream a whole set at once. The ordinary path spends one command per light out of about ten a second, so seven bulbs flicker at barely 1 Hz each; streaming sends one frame for the whole area, so the speed stops being divided - up to 25 Hz, and each light in the area can run a different pattern at the same time.
Reads each bulb's colour and brightness before it starts and puts it back when the flicker stops, even if the container restarted mid-run. Optional console password. Restarts itself if it ever stops responding.
Talks directly to your Hue Bridge over the local API - no Philips cloud account. Everything is configured in the web UI; there are no environment variables to set.
First run: open the WebUI, auto-discover your bridge or type its IP, then press the link button on the bridge and hit Pair within 30 seconds. If discovery or pairing fails on the default bridge network, switch Network Type to Host and try again.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: hue philips lighting flicker lightstyle quake doom entertainment ambient rgb bridge
Container.Requires: A Philips Hue Bridge on the same network, reachable by IP. Pairing needs one press of the bridge's physical link button. Nothing else: no Philips account, no cloud service, and no environment variables to set.
Container.Changes:
### 1.0.0
First Community Applications release.
- 64 presets across twenty games, each carrying its own speed, brightness range and colour. - Entertainment streaming at up to 25 Hz, with a different pattern per light in one area. - Custom a-z lightstyles with a live waveform preview, exportable as JSON. - Restores every bulb's colour and brightness when the flicker stops, across a restart. - Optional console password, and a health check that restarts the container if it stops responding.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the flicker console web UI. Defaults to 26000 (Quake's own port) to stay clear of the usual 8080 crowd.

Config.Name: Port (host networking only)
Config.Description: Only used with Network Type set to Host, where the port mapping above does nothing and this is the only way to move the listener. Leave it alone on bridge networking.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Holds config.json: your bridge pairing, saved custom patterns, console password and settings. Keep this mapped or you will have to re-pair with the bridge after every update.
